title: Committee of Supply – Head Q (Ministry of Communications and Information)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head Q (Ministry of Communications and Information)

sections.label: Tech job vacancies and talent schemes
sections.summary: Tech job vacancies have doubled since 2010, and the Government has introduced schemes such as TeSa, SGUnited Jobs & Skills and the PCP to strengthen the talent pool.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Today, the number of tech-related job vacancies is double that of the number in 2010, according to a recent report by the Boston Consulting Group.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: As we continue to attract large tech firms to Singapore and as we digitally transform our Singapore enterprises, the need for talents cannot be more pressing.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: I am heartened that the Government has introduced many useful schemes such as TeSa, SGUnited Jobs & Skills and the PCP, that help to strengthen our talent pool with the requisite technical knowledge and industry skillsets.

sections.label: Gender gap in tech manpower
sections.summary: 2017 MCI manpower statistics showed 68% male and 32% female, while women held 29% of tech-related degrees versus 53% of overall degrees.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: The 2017 manpower statistics for MCI reported a distinct gender gap with male at 68% and female at 32%.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: Drawing comparisons from the same Boston Consulting Group report that I mentioned earlier, the composition of women with tech-related degrees is 29% and this is less than the 53% representation in overall degrees.

sections.label: Support for local innovation start-ups
sections.summary: The speaker asks what plans will help local start-ups and companies in the innovation sector secure significant projects within and outside the public sector.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling (MacPherson)
sentences.text: On the support for innovation, apart from the announced Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2025 Plan (RIE2025) to boost R&D, I would like to ask the Government what plans will be put in place to help local start-ups or local companies in the innovation sector to secure significant projects within and outside the public sector that can boost their credibility.

sections.label: Digitalisation for businesses post-COVID-19
sections.summary: Digitalisation for businesses is no longer an option after COVID-19.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Digitalisation for businesses is no longer an option post-COVID-19.

sections.label: CTO-as-a-service resource pooling
sections.summary: Hiring an in-house IT expert could be costly given their scale, so the announced CTO-as-a-service idea of pooling resources sounds very good.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Also, hiring an in-house IT expert, given their scale, could be costly.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Therefore, the idea of pooling resources and having CTO-as-a-service as announced during this year’s Budget sounds like a very good idea.

sections.label: SMEs Go Digital deadline problems
sections.summary: A local tech solution provider said many local MSMEs gave up purchasing its solutions because the strictly imposed deadline and slow application processing risked missing the deadline.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: For example, a local tech solution provider recently shared with me that many local MSMEs expressed interest to purchase its solutions because of the SMEs Go Digital funding.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: But because the deadline was strictly imposed and the application processing took a while, a number of these companies gave up for fear of missing the deadline by the time the application is approved, if it is approved.

sections.label: Information communications sector professionals needed
sections.summary: The information communications sector would need another 60,000 professionals over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: The information communications sector would need another 60,000 professionals over the next three years.

sections.label: Post-pandemic economy and digitalisation pilot trap
sections.summary: Only then can we be fully poised to take advantage of post-pandemic world economy opportunities, and a McKinsey report indicated 85% of ASEAN companies are stuck in a digitalisation pilot trap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Only then, can we be fully poised to take full advantage of the opportunities emerging from the post-pandemic world economy.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: It is noteworthy that the recent McKinsey report indicated that 85% of ASEAN companies are still stuck in this digitalisation pilot trap.

sections.label: Go Digital Programme assists SMEs
sections.summary: The Go Digital Programme has assisted a lot of SMEs through their digital journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: The Go Digital Programme has assisted a lot of SMEs through their digital journey.

sections.label: Unequal SME digitalisation progress
sections.summary: Not all SMEs have made equal progress in digitalisation, and the pandemic has widened the gap between digital haves and have-nots.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: However, not all SMEs have made equal progress in digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: This pandemic has widened the gap between the digital haves and the digital have-nots.

sections.label: SMEs employment, GDP and digitisation
sections.summary: SMEs provide employment to about 70% of the workforce and contribute almost 50% of Singapore's GDP, with digitisation and e-commerce as potential areas, and digital transformation has become imperative for some SMEs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, SMEs provide employment to about 70% of our workforce and contribute almost 50% of Singapore's GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: The digitisation of SME's business processes and the growing trend in e-commerce are two potential areas where SMEs can tap on in order to increase efficiency as well as to grow their businesses.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin (Potong Pasir)
sentences.text: We have also seen, in the past year, under the backdrop of the COVID-19 pandemic, that digital transformation has become an imperative step that some SMEs have to urgently take.

sections.label: Budget focus on SME digitisation
sections.summary: The focus on SME digitisation in the Budget is welcome, with new initiatives and increased support levels for existing initiatives.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The focus on SME digitisation in the Budget is welcome, with new initiatives as well as increased support levels for existing initiatives.

sections.label: China JD Spark programme
sections.summary: China's JD Spark programme provides supply chain, business support and credit to bring stalls and shops online, plus flexible employment in poorer regions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In China, for example, the JD "Spark" programme provides supply chain, business support and credit to bring stalls and shops online as well as flexible employment and work from home opportunities in poorer regions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I hope the Government will elaborate on the take-up and effectiveness of the SME digitisation programmes that are being extended—and the lessons that have been learnt to date.

sections.label: SMEs employment and GDP
sections.summary: SMEs, including hawkers, employ two thirds of the workforce and contribute almost half of GDP.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, SMEs, which include the hawkers, provide employment for two thirds of our workforce and contribute to almost half of our GDP.

sections.label: Digitalisation programme take-up rates
sections.summary: The question asks whether take-up rates changed and what utilisation rates were for SME Digital Tech Hub, pre-approved solutions and Digital Resilience Bonus.

sentences.speaker: Mr Don Wee (Chua Chu Kang)
sentences.text: Has the Ministry observed any changes in the take-up rates of the digitalisation programmes and what has been the utilisation rates of the various services such as SME Digital Tech Hub consultancy services and pre-approved solutions and the Digital Resilience Bonus?

sections.label: Singapore 5G approach and plans
sections.summary: The question asks Singapore's approach and plans for 5G to benefit consumers, businesses and society while minimising risks.

sentences.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo (East Coast)
sentences.text: What is Singapore's approach and plans for 5G to ensure that consumers, businesses and the wider society benefit from 5G deployment while minimising the associated risks?

sections.label: Data privacy and protection bill
sections.summary: Growth of IoT, AI, gig economy and tech giants puts privacy in the spotlight, and the House passed the Personal Data Protection Amendment Bill 2020.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: The growth of the Internet of Things, Artificial Intelligence, the gig economy and global tech giants, means that the race for data and data-centric technologies firmly puts the issue of privacy in the spotlight.

sentences.speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: We have been cognisant of this and recently this House passed the Personal Data Protection Amendment Bill 2020 to hold organisations accountable for the data they handle.

sections.label: Cybersecurity lapses among residents
sections.summary: In the past year, a quarter of Singapore residents suffered at least one cybersecurity lapse, most commonly unauthorised attempts to access online accounts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: In the past year, a quarter of Singapore residents suffered at least one cybersecurity lapse, with unauthorised attempts to access online accounts being most common.

sections.label: Singtel cyber breach reminder
sections.summary: The recent cyber breach at Singtel shows that even well-resourced major corporations are at risk as new technology is adopted.

sentences.speaker: Mr Alex Yam
sentences.text: The recent cyber breach at Singtel is a stark reminder that even as we adopt new technology, major corporations with a wealth of resources are also at risk.

sections.label: Global and ASEAN digital economy
sections.summary: The global digital economy is worth almost $3 trillion, and within ASEAN it is expected to grow to $197 billion by 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: Chairman, the global digital economy today is worth almost $3 trillion.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong)
sentences.text: And within ASEAN, this is expected to grow to $197 billion by 2025.

sections.label: SingPost universal service obligation
sections.summary: SingPost is required to perform a set of universal service obligation as determined by IMDA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: SingPost is required to perform a set of universal service obligation as determined by IMDA.

sections.label: E-commerce volume growth trend
sections.summary: E-commerce volume is expected to grow between 12% to 20% annually for the next five years, and both trends are expected to intensify.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: I expect both trends to intensify in the coming years.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sitoh Yih Pin
sentences.text: I understand that e-commerce volume is expected to grow between 12% to 20% annually for the next five years.

sections.label: Digital adoption in tenancy agreements
sections.summary: MCI is asked whether it can incorporate digital adoption like digital payment solutions into new tenancy agreements and renewals, with rental relief in return.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Can MCI incorporate certain digital adoption like digital payment solutions as a condition into new tenancy agreements and renewals, providing rental relief measures in return for digital adoption?

sections.label: Non-contact delivery methods expansion
sections.summary: There is a need to expand non-contact delivery methods like collection points with real-time tracking to minimise delivery disruptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: To overcome this challenge, there is a need to expand the use of non-contact delivery methods like collections points with real-time tracking to minimise delivery disruptions.

sections.label: Circular economy for parcels
sections.summary: MCI is asked whether it has considered a circular economy on parcels through delivery, return and recycle.

sentences.speaker: Mr Edward Chia Bing Hui (Holland-Bukit Timah)
sentences.text: Has MCI considered a circular economy on parcels through the process of delivery, return and recycle?

sections.label: Promoting reading and affordable e-books
sections.summary: Reading brings people together, and the Ministry is asked how to promote reading through easy access and affordable e-books.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It also plays an important role in bringing family and friends together as many of us would have experienced the joy of discussing or sharing a favourite book with fellow readers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: It is therefore important for any progressive society to nurture a love of reading and lifelong learning in its people." In this regard, I wish to ask the Ministry, in today's digital world, how can we promote reading through easy access and ensuring that the e-books remain affordable for all?

sections.label: Books and e-books for inmates
sections.summary: The Ministry is asked to work with the Singapore Prison Service to offer inmates a wider range of books including e-books.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: Further, during my recent visits to Prisons, I have come to understand that the Singapore Prison Service has begun to offer tablets to inmates for them to draft emails to their family members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Hany Soh (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
sentences.text: To better facilitate rehabilitations and integrations for education, skills upgrading and enhance employability skills, can the Ministry work with the Singapore Prison Service to offer a wider range of books including e-books to the inmates?

sections.label: Digitalisation and the social compact
sections.summary: It asks what can be done so digitalisation does not derail efforts to strengthen the social compact and leave the vulnerable behind.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Given this unintended but inevitable consequence of the pandemic, what can we do to ensure that digitalisation does not derail our efforts in strengthening our social compact?

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: How do we ensure that the vulnerable ones amongst us are not by default technological laggards, as this only further entrenches their social and financial positions?

sections.label: Cybersecurity training and mobile access for seniors
sections.summary: Cybersecurity continues to be emphasised in training programmes with seniors, and low-cost mobile plans were rolled out under Mobile Access for Seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: He also highlighted that cybersecurity was something that would continue to be emphasised in the training programmes with seniors.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It was reported that the programme aimed to reach out to 100,000 seniors by this month.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There had been roll-outs of low cost mobile phone plans for seniors through a scheme called Mobile Access for Seniors, aimed at the low-income.

sections.label: One-to-one laptop provision
sections.summary: MOE has aimed for a one-to-one laptop provision for all Secondary school students by 2021.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: MOE has aimed for a one-to-one laptop provision for all Secondary school students by 2021.

sections.label: Broadband penetration and unconnected households
sections.summary: Minister Iswaran said household broadband penetration rose from 87% in 2014 to 98% in 2019, leaving about 27,000 of 1.37 million resident households without broadband access.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: On 2 February this year, Minister Iswaran informed the House that under the Home Access and NEU PC Plus Programmes, Singapore’s household-level broadband penetration rate has increased from 87% in 2014 to 98% in 2019.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are 1.37 million resident households in Singapore according to the statistics.

sentences.speaker: Dr Shahira Abdullah (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: This would translate to about 27,000 households not having broadband access – no small number.

sections.label: COVID-19 digital divide, low-income households
sections.summary: COVID-19 has accentuated digital gains and divides, and the member asks how the Ministry helps low-income households access digital tools and stay connected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, COVID-19 has accentuated digital gains, but also digital divides in our communities.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: How is the Ministry helping low-income households to access digital tools or platforms and remain connected with the wider society?

sections.label: E-commerce scams during pandemic
sections.summary: E-commerce scams were the most common online scams and increased significantly during this pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng
sentences.text: E-commerce scams were the most common among online scams and it has increased significantly during this pandemic.

sections.label: Unequal digital access and literacy
sections.summary: Despite efforts to improve digital literacy, not all Singaporeans have equal access to digital devices or are digitally literate, and the pandemic has widened the gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, although a lot efforts have been made to improve digital literacy, not all Singaporeans have equal access to digital devices and are digitally literate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
sentences.text: This pandemic has widened the gap between the digital haves versus the digital have-nots.

sections.label: Update on digitalisation programmes and engagement
sections.summary: The member asks for an update on programmes helping Singaporeans keep pace with digitalisation, measures to bridge the digital gap for the vulnerable, and plans to engage Singaporeans in developing digital services.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: In this regard, I would like to ask the Ministry for an update on the progress on efforts made over the past months on the various programmes to help Singaporeans keep pace with the country’s digitalisation efforts.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: In particular, what measures are put in place to bridge the digital gap in ensuring that the vulnerable do not fall through the gaps due to a lack of awareness and resources.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: Lastly, I would also like to ask the Government what plans might there be in engaging Singaporeans more when developing digital services to meet their needs?

sections.label: Government messages for mother tongue and illiterate seniors
sections.summary: The member asks what steps ensure those who understand only mother tongues receive comprehensible Government messages, and how illiterate seniors will be communicated with electronically.

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: What are the steps taken by the Government to ensure that those who can only understand mother tongues are able to receive Government messages in a manner they can comprehend?

sentences.speaker: Ms Tin Pei Ling
sentences.text: And for seniors who are illiterate, how does the Government plan to electronically communicate with them?

sections.label: SME digital adoption numbers
sections.summary: Over 63,000 SMEs adopted digital solutions under SMEs Go Digital, with 40,000 signing up in 2020, plus e-commerce, advisory and e-invoicing uptake.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Today, more than 63,000 SMEs have adopted digital solutions with the support of the SMEs Go Digital programme which was launched in 2017.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: About 40,000 of them, in fact, signed up just last year and 2020 alone.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: At least 2,000 enterprises have gained access to overseas markets through e-commerce platforms under the Grow Digital scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Over 1,000 enterprises have engaged the SME Digital Tech Hub for advice and over 35,000 enterprises are now registered for e-invoicing, compared to 1,000 a year ago.

sections.label: Digital Leaders Programme support
sections.summary: The new Digital Leaders Programme provides up to 70% support on qualifying costs for firms to build a core digital team.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The new Digital Leaders Programme (DLP) that we have launched aims to equip firms with the capabilities and talent to accelerate their digital transformation journey.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: This programme will provide up to 70% support on qualifying costs to help companies build a core digital team to develop and execute their digitalisation strategy.

sections.label: Accreditation@SGD tech companies
sections.summary: Accreditation@SGD recognises local tech companies whose products Government agencies consider first for ICT procurement, with a SecureTech track added in 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: IMDA's Accreditation@SGD programme recognises promising and innovative local tech companies, and their products are considered first by Government agencies for ICT procurement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In 2019, IMDA and Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA) launched a new SecureTech track under the Accreditation programme to help local cybersecurity programmes gain greater access to Government projects.

sections.label: Better Data-Driven Business programme
sections.summary: IMDA will launch the Better Data-Driven Business programme to help businesses better use data and serve customers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: To help businesses better use of data and better serve their customers, IMDA will launch the Better Data-Driven Business programme, or BDDB.

sections.label: 5G nationwide coverage plans
sections.summary: 5G will be the backbone of Singapore's digital infrastructure, with at least 50% standalone outdoor coverage by end-2021 and nationwide by end-2025.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Beyond scaling up our efforts to help companies go digital, we must continue to search for technology solutions that can power the next bound of our economic growth and strengthen our position as hub for digital innovation. 5G is key to this as it will be the backbone of our digital infrastructure and Singapore will have at least 50% 5G standalone outdoor coverage by the end of next year, and nationwide coverage by the end of 2025.

sections.label: Platform challenges and investment
sections.summary: Over 190 challenges were launched and over 60 solutions developed, with $50 million to be invested over five years to enhance the platform.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Over 190 challenges have been launched, and over 60 solutions have been successfully developed.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We will invest $50 million over the next five years to enhance the capabilities of this platform.

sections.label: SGUnited Jobs and TeSA placements
sections.summary: Over 18,000 ICT opportunities were available under SGUnited Jobs and Skills, and over 8,000 Singaporeans were placed in ICT jobs through TeSA since 2016.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Under the SGUnited Jobs and Skills programmes, there were more than 18,000 available opportunities in the Information and Communications sector as at the end of last year; of that, more than 10,000 were for jobs openings.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Since 2016, over 8,000 Singaporeans from fresh graduates to mid-career professionals, have been placed in good ICT jobs through the TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) programme.

sections.label: TeSA Mid-Career Advance programme
sections.summary: The TeSA Mid-Career Advance programme was launched last year to train and transition workers in their 40s and 50s into tech jobs.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Last year, we also launched the TeSA Mid-Career Advance programme to train and transition workers in their 40s and 50s into tech jobs.

sections.label: SG Digital Office and hawker e-payments
sections.summary: The SG Digital Office was established in June last year and about 10,000 hawkers and stallholders have adopted e-payment solutions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: That is why we established the SG Digital Office in June last year, and launched the Hawkers and Seniors Go Digital programmes.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: So far, about 10,000 hawkers – of a base of about, I think 18,000 or so – and stallholders have adopted e-payment solutions.

sections.label: Seniors trained in digital skills
sections.summary: The SG Digital Office has trained about 69,000 seniors in digital skills and measures to safeguard against Internet risks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The SG Digital Office has trained about 69,000 seniors in digital skills as well as measures to safeguard themselves against risks on the Internet.

sections.label: Increase in e-database and digital loans
sections.summary: Since April last year, e-database usage rose 145% and digital loans rose 32%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: As a result, since April last year, there has been a 145% increase in e-database usage and a 32% increase in digital loans.

sections.label: SolarWinds cyberattack affected organisations
sections.summary: The SolarWinds cyberattack uncovered in December last year affected about 18,000 organisations, including US government agencies and Fortune 500 companies.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Members would recall the SolarWinds cyberattack uncovered in December last year, which affected about 18,000 organisations, including US government agencies and Fortune 500 companies.

sections.label: Gov.sg platform expansion
sections.summary: Gov.sg expanded to 10 platforms with over 2.5 million subscribers, and its WhatsApp channel grew from 7,000 to 1.2 million subscribers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: In addition, Gov.sg was expanded to 10 platforms, including Telegram, Instagram and TikTok, and we now have more than 2.5 million subscribers across these platforms.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The Gov.sg WhatsApp channel grew exponentially from 7,000 subscribers in January 2020 to 1.2 million today.

sections.label: TechSkills Accelerator company commitments
sections.summary: Under TeSA, companies including Google, Microsoft, IBM, Singtel, Sea and Grab committed to over 5,000 technology and ICT jobs and skills opportunities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Under the TechSkills Accelerator (TeSA) initiative, companies such as Google, Microsoft, IBM, Singtel, Sea and Grab have committed to create more than 5,000 jobs and skills opportunities in technology and ICT.

sections.label: Digital for Life movement launch
sections.summary: President Halimah Yaacob launched the Digital for Life movement and Fund, targeting $10 million in three years with dollar-for-dollar government matching.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: Last month, to that end, President Halimah Yaacob launched the Digital for Life movement in conjunction with the President's Challenge 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The movement is part of a wider national effort to bring together the people, private and public sectors to foster digital skills, digital wellness and digital access among all Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: We have also established the Digital for Life Fund, which will support projects contributing to the goals of the Digital for Life movement.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: The target is to grow the fund to $10 million over the next three years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: All cash donations will be matched, dollar for dollar, by the Government.

sections.label: Ministry digital future plans
sections.summary: The Ministry will invest in infrastructure, research and digital innovation, equip businesses with digital tools, and support Singaporeans to learn and upskill.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Communications and Information (Mr S Iswaran)
sentences.text: My Ministry will lay strong foundations for that digital future by investing in infrastructure, driving research and digital innovation, equipping businesses with digital tools and supporting Singaporeans to learn, upskill and stay informed.

sections.label: Nationwide 5G standalone networks
sections.summary: Standalone 5G networks are a policy priority, with at least 50% outdoor coverage by end of next year and nationwide coverage by end of 2025.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Looking ahead, we will need world-class, secure and resilient 5G networks.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: It was thus a policy priority for our nationwide 5G networks to be standalone – new standalone networks, 5G all the way through, from end to end. 5G standalone networks unlock the full suite of capabilities, including network slicing and ultra-reliable low latency communications, necessary for applications such as cloud gaming and smart factories. 5G deployment has started and by the end of next year, we will have at least 50% standalone outdoor coverage for 5G.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Nationwide 5G standalone coverage will arrive by the end of 2025.

sections.label: E-commerce scams and losses
sections.summary: E-commerce scams are the most common scam type in Singapore, rising almost 20% from 2019, with victims losing over $200 million last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In Singapore the most common type of scams relates to e-commerce and these increased by almost 20% from 2019.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Overall, victims to scams lost more than $200 million last year.

sections.label: Blocked suspected scam calls
sections.summary: 28 million suspected scam calls were blocked in the fourth quarter of last year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As a result, 28 million suspected scam calls were blocked in the fourth quarter of last year.

sections.label: Singtel FTA breach files
sections.summary: Singtel reported that some files were taken in a breach of FTA, a third-party file sharing system it uses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Closer to home, Singtel reported that some files were taken as a result of a breach to FTA, a third-party file sharing system that Singtel uses.

sections.label: CII Supply Chain Programme
sections.summary: A CII Supply Chain Programme is being developed as a partnership involving CSA, CII owners and their vendors.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: To this end, we are developing a CII Supply Chain Programme – a partnership involving all stakeholders – Cyber Security Agency of Singapore (CSA), CII owners, and their vendors.

sections.label: SG Cyber Safe Programme
sections.summary: As part of the Safer Cyberspace Masterplan, CSA will launch the SG Cyber Safe Programme to help companies strengthen cybersecurity.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Cyberattacks on companies have a far reaching impact on our wider economy.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: So, as part of the Safer Cyberspace Masterplan, CSA will launch the SG Cyber Safe Programme to support companies in strengthening their cybersecurity.

sections.label: Trustmark stakeholder engagement
sections.summary: CSA will engage stakeholders on the specifics of this Trustmark from April this year.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: CSA will engage stakeholders regarding the specifics of this Trustmark from April this year.

sections.label: Cyber talent and leaders programmes
sections.summary: Youths are encouraged through SG Cyber Talent, and SG Cyber Leaders was launched to groom world-class cybersecurity leaders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Second, to strengthen our talent pipeline for the longer term, we encourage youths to pursue a career in the field through cyber outreach initiatives like SG Cyber Talent.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: And thirdly, to groom world-class cybersecurity leaders, we launched the SG Cyber Leaders programme to create a community for current and developing cyber leaders to exchange ideas, and learn about global best practices.

sections.label: International cyber norms cooperation
sections.summary: Singapore works with UN and ASEAN partners to develop and implement norms for responsible state behaviour, as cyber threats are global and transborder.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: As cyber threats are global and transborder, we are working closely with international partners across the UN and ASEAN to develop and implement norms for responsible state behaviour.

sections.label: Singapore AI governance framework
sections.summary: Singapore takes an open, collaborative approach to AI governance, and launched the second edition of its Model AI Governance Framework in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: In terms of AI governance, Singapore takes an open and collaborative approach to govern the use of AI, recognising that we need to safeguard consumers’ interest and facilitate innovation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We launched the second edition of the Model AI Governance Framework in 2020, which incorporates feedback and examples from international and local companies across a diverse set of sectors, in response to the first edition of the Framework.

sections.label: Digital Economy Agreements for digital trade
sections.summary: Singapore pioneered Digital Economy Agreements to create new norms and rules for cross-border digital transactions, building on existing networks and initiatives.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: While our existing trade agreements meet the needs of traditional trade in goods and services, we recognise the need for new norms and rules to support cross-border digital transactions like e-invoicing, data flows, digital identities.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: This is why Singapore pioneered Digital Economy Agreements, or DEAs, building on our existing networks and initiatives.

sections.label: ASEAN data protection frameworks
sections.summary: Singapore led development of ASEAN Model Contractual Clauses for cross-border personal data transfers and an ASEAN Data Management Framework for businesses.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: Regionally, Singapore led the development of ASEAN Model Contractual Clauses, terms and conditions that may be included in legally binding contracts for the transfer of personal data across borders.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
sentences.text: We also led the development of an ASEAN Data Management Framework – a guide for businesses to implement a data management system with appropriate data protection safeguards.

sections.label: Heartlands Go Digital communication efforts
sections.summary: Singapore will strengthen communication efforts to make trusted information accessible, and helped small companies adopt digital solutions through Heartlands Go Digital.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Fourth, we will strengthen our communication efforts, making trusted information accessible to all.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: We stepped up efforts to help small companies, including mom-and-pop HDB shops, to adopt simple digital solutions through the Heartlands Go Digital initiative.

sections.label: Digital connectivity subsidy programmes
sections.summary: IMDA's Home Access and NEU PC Plus programmes subsidised digital connectivity for 20,000 low-income families last year, and were enhanced in 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Last year, IMDA’s Home Access and NEU PC Plus programmes, which subsidise digital connectivity for low-income households, benefited 20,000 families.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The two programmes were enhanced in 2020, providing faster broadband speeds and more bundled device options.

sections.label: Digital access for students and seniors
sections.summary: MCI works with MOE on students' digital access and literacy, and over 6,400 seniors have benefited from the Mobile Access for Low-Income Seniors scheme.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: MCI also works closely with MOE to address digital access and literacy needs of students.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: I am glad to update Ms Sylvia Lim that since the Mobile Access for Low-Income Seniors scheme was launched last year, more than 6,400 seniors have benefited from the subsidised smartphones and mobile data plans.

sections.label: Digital for Life movement launch
sections.summary: Calls for collective action to bridge the digital gap led to the launch of the Digital for Life movement last month.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Many asked what we, as a society, can do to help bridge the digital gap.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: It was this and other similar calls for collective action that led us to launch the Digital for Life movement last month, which Minister Iswaran mentioned.

sections.label: Geylang East library seniors pilot
sections.summary: The pilot at Geylang East Public Library helping seniors navigate online public services will be evaluated before a further rollout is decided.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The pilot at the Geylang East Public Library to help seniors navigate online public services will be evaluated and a further rollout will be decided upon once we see the results.

sections.label: NLB book donations to inmates
sections.summary: Last year NLB donated more than 7,000 books to cater to inmates' varying reading needs.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Last year, NLB donated more than 7,000 books to cater to inmates’ varying reading needs.

sections.label: Locker convenience survey result
sections.summary: Ninety-six percent agreed the lockers will bring them convenience and that they will use the locker stations in their neighbourhoods.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Ninety-six percent agreed that the lockers will bring them convenience and they will use the locker stations in their neighbourhoods.

sections.label: Parcel locker network launch and emissions
sections.summary: The parcel locker network is expected to cut daily delivery distance travelled by 44%, and Pick is on track to launch up to 200 locker stations by April.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Mr Edward Chia would be pleased to know that the parcel locker network is expected to reduce distance travelled for delivery by 44% daily, and this will go a long way towards reducing carbon emissions.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Pick is on track to launch the first batch of up to 200 locker stations by April.

sections.label: Citizen Translators volunteer initiative
sections.summary: The Citizen Translators initiative reaches out to volunteers to co-create solutions for the most suitable renderings.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The first initiative is Citizen Translators, where we reach out to volunteers to co-create solutions for the most suitable renderings.

sections.label: Tamil Engine for SG Translate
sections.summary: The Tamil Engine for SG Translate was launched last October.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The second initiative is the Tamil Engine for SG Translate, which was launched last October.

sections.label: SingPass mobile app translation plans
sections.summary: The Government plans to translate the SingPass mobile app by June 2021.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: The Government also has plans to translate the SingPass mobile app by June 2021.

sections.label: Digital Leaders' Programme and CTO service
sections.summary: The Minister announced the launch of the Digital Leaders' Programme and “CTO as a service” for companies.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: For companies, the Minister has announced that we will be launching the Digital Leaders' Programme and “CTO as a service”.

sections.label: Digital Ambassadors teaching seniors online safety
sections.summary: Digital Ambassadors teach seniors to protect themselves online, such as using strong passwords and not disclosing one-time passwords.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Communications and Information (Ms Sim Ann)
sentences.text: Digital Ambassadors have been engaging and teaching seniors how they can protect themselves when transacting online so that they do not fall victim to scams, for example, to use strong passwords for online accounts and not disclose one-time passwords when using digital banking services.

sections.label: Technology-related investments flowing into Singapore
sections.summary: Singapore has seen more technology-related investments and new projects from big global tech players.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The second thing is we have also seen the flow into Singapore of more technology-related investments.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Again, I think that is in recognition of both the business conducive environment that we have in Singapore, the talent base that we have in Singapore and the opportunity set that they see in our region, and how Singapore can be the locale from which those opportunities can be accessed.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, we have seen significant investments and new projects initiated by the big tech players, global tech players.

sections.label: Scarcity of tech talent
sections.summary: The passage states that tech talent is scarce across areas such as AI, cybersecurity and data analytics, so Singapore needs its fair share.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Because of that scarcity of tech talent across the spectrum – whether you are talking about AI, cybersecurity, data analytics and so on – we need our fair share of talent.

sections.label: IMDA digital talent collaboration
sections.summary: IMDA and other economic agencies, including Enterprise Singapore, will work with companies already on their digital journey that have a core digital talent team.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Basically, we are starting on this because we believe that there is a value proposition here.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And, so, IMDA, working with other economic agencies, in particular, Enterprise Singapore, will be focused on working with companies that had already embarked on their digital journey; somewhat progressed in the way they have evolved their systems, and they also have the kernel, the core of a digital talent team, so that this can be the foundation upon which we build this.

sections.label: Agencies identify companies, no quota
sections.summary: Agencies will work with companies they deal with to identify them, and there is no preset quota for particular sectors.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, this will be something where the agencies will be working with companies that they deal with, in order to identify.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: There is no preset quota for particular sectors.

sections.label: First cluster: illegal online businesses
sections.summary: The first cluster of issues concerns websites or online businesses that may be outright illegal or in a grey area.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The conversations are still on-going but I can share a few clusters of issues that have already emerged from our discussions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The first cluster of issues would concern websites or online businesses that, on one hand, may be outright illegal, in terms of proffering sexual services, or they could be part of a grey area in which, perhaps, behaviour could be encouraged, which then may move down the slippery slope towards criminal activities.

sections.label: Second cluster: non-consensual image sharing
sections.summary: The second cluster of issues concerns the sharing to many and without consent of images and footage of victims.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The second cluster of issues that have emerged concern the sharing to many and without consent of images and footage of victims.

sections.label: Third cluster: one-on-one interactions
sections.summary: The third cluster of issues concerns one-on-one interactions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
sentences.text: The third cluster of issues concern one-on-one interactions.

sections.label: Resourcing and evaluating customisation schemes
sections.summary: The speaker hopes the schemes will be adequately resourced and frequently evaluated for effectiveness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: Mass customisation is notoriously difficult, even with technology.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar
sentences.text: So, I hope that these schemes will truly, really, be adequately resourced, which does involve cost, and evaluated frequently on their effectiveness and what needs to be done differently.

sections.label: Supporting Singapore SMEs at every stage
sections.summary: With over 200,000 SME entities in Singapore, the objective is baseline support from start-up to scale-up and beyond.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: When we talk about SMEs in Singapore, we are talking about north of 200,000 entities.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, our objective is, on the one hand, to have that baseline support, so that SMEs can start the journey.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: Hence, my point in what I said earlier, that we are committed to supporting businesses at every stage, from start-up to scale-up, and those even further beyond.

sections.label: CTO-as-a-Service for SME customisation
sections.summary: Newer initiatives build on existing capabilities for greater customisation, with CTO-as-a-Service giving SMEs access to expertise for diagnostics and strategy.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: The newer initiatives that we have embarked on are really trying to build on that suite of capabilities that we have, to allow a greater level of customisation but without overstating the case because the challenge remains.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: So, for example, CTO-as-a-Service really can go a lot deeper because you now have access as an SME to people with the expertise to do the diagnostics, assess the need and more than that to work out a strategy and a plan.

sections.label: Digital Leaders' Programme customisation
sections.summary: The Digital Leaders' Programme is even more customised and works at a higher level.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: At the same time, we have got something on the Digital Leaders' Programme which is even more customised; working at a higher level.

sections.label: Omni-channel strategy for physical libraries
sections.summary: The experience is not to be eliminated but enhanced through an omni-channel strategy where digital platforms reinforce the physical library's value.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: I think it is not an experience that we want to eliminate by any means.

sentences.speaker: Mr S Iswaran
sentences.text: And actually, what we want to do is enhance it by creating what we describe as an omni-channel strategy so that the digital platform and the digital initiatives will reinforce the attractiveness and the value of what you have physically in the library.
